evidence: src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts:2 `import { Request } from 'express';` brings in a web framework type from the express package.

src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts:20 `async eventsOf(loanId: string, request?: Request): Promise<LoanEvent[]>`: a domain method signature takes an express HTTP Request, which belongs to presentation.

src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts:13 `constructor(private readonly db: PrismaService)`: PrismaService is declared in src/persistence, which business may depend on, so this is allowed wiring.
Lines 17 and 21 call `this.db.loanEvent.create`/`findMany` through the allowed persistence class PrismaService, so these flags are not misplaced I/O.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file sits in the business layer, which is a domain layer. Its method `eventsOf(loanId: string, request?: Request)` takes `Request` from the 'express' web package. That is an HTTP request type, which belongs to the transport/presentation layer. The rubric says a request type in a domain signature fails even when the parameter is optional or unused, as it is here.

The two domain-does-io flags (`create` at line 17 and `findMany` at line 21) don't count. Both calls go through the injected `PrismaService`. The project declares that class itself in `src/persistence`, and the layer model lets business depend on persistence. The rubric says calls into a class of an allowed layer are not misplaced I/O. The `PrismaService` constructor parameter is just dependency wiring.

The `LoanEvent` interface and the counter logic are fine for a domain file.

violations.message: Domain method `eventsOf(loanId: string, request?: Request)` takes `Request` from the 'express' package. That is an HTTP request type that belongs in the presentation layer, and it doesn't belong in a business/domain signature even though it is optional and unused.
